paragraphs.source_en: The world’s hunger for leadership has been growing for years. There is no doubt that a charismatic new leader took the world stage on November 4, 2008, with the election of Barack Obama as president of the United States. On the night of his victory, millions of Americans wept with pride in their country and relief that he had triumphed over old prejudices. Watching on television, children cheered in the Indonesian grade school the president-elect had attended as a child. Brits raised pints in countless pubs, and Kenyans danced with Obama’s relatives in the village where his father was born. But Barack Obama’s presidency is in its earliest days, and what we have now is the hope that he will become one of the giants. One result of Barack Obama’s extraordinary election is to remind us of just how thin our leadership bench is. Most of the leaders we once revered are gone.

Gandhi, the Kennedys, Martin Luther King, Jr.—all were slain.
